macros.name: bnfes
macros.doc: The \bnfes command gives the symbol for the empty string.

macros.name: bnfmore
macros.doc: A production can be continued on addition lines by \bnfmore or \bnfmore*, which respectively give a numbered or unnumbered line in the bnf environment.

macros.name: bnfmore*
macros.doc: A production can be continued on addition lines by \bnfmore or \bnfmore*, which respectively give a numbered or unnumbered line in the bnf environment.

macros.name: bnfor
macros.doc: The \bnfor command generates the OR symbol, and the \bnfsp command introduces a space.

macros.name: bnfpn
macros.doc: The \bnfpn command generates a production name.

macros.name: bnfprod
macros.doc: Each BNF production is defined by a \bnfprod command, which has two arguments giving its left and right sides.

macros.name: bnfprod*
macros.doc: Each BNF production is defined by a \bnfprod command, which has two arguments giving its left and right sides.

macros.name: bnfsk
macros.doc: Some literal terminal strings can be abbreviated with the ‘skip’ token, which is generated by the \bnfsk command.

macros.name: bnfsp
macros.doc: The \bnfor command generates the OR symbol, and the \bnfsp command introduces a space.

macros.name: bnftd
macros.doc: The \bnftd command generates a descriptive phrase, as an alternative to a literal string.

envs.name: bnf
envs.doc: BNF productions are defined in a bnf or bnf* environment, which respectively give numbered or unnumbered lists of productions.

envs.name: bnf*
envs.doc: BNF productions are defined in a bnf or bnf* environment, which respectively give numbered or unnumbered lists of productions.
